narration.text: These are the Neptun Baths in the Fabric district, designed by László Székely and opened in the years before the First World War. Look at the roofline and decorative details, a playful Secession take on a public bathhouse.
narration.history: Fabric grew as an industrial and commercial district along the Bega, and the city invested in modern public facilities in the early 1900s.
narration.why_it_matters: The baths show that Secession style was used not only for homes and palaces but also for everyday civic buildings.
